title: Research supercomputing from K to Fugaku

inventory.name: Fugaku
inventory.region: RIKEN Center for Computational Science, Kobe, Japan
inventory.claim: RIKEN suspended Fugaku operations and external access on 14 November, confirmed in its 17 November notice. Shared use had begun in March 2021.
inventory.limit: As of 17 November the operator gave no restart date. November TOP500 lists rank 9 and carries the 442.01 PFlop/s HPL result first published in November 2020.

inventory.name: JUPITER Booster
inventory.claim: Jülich reported that more than 500 projects had received JUPITER compute time since installation in 2025 and identified results already produced on the system. The Booster retained 1.000 EFlop/s measured HPL at rank 5 in November 2026.
inventory.limit: Status refers to evidenced allocated research access on the Booster. JSC user documentation describes early access and the separate CPU Cluster module remained in phased rollout.

inventory.name: FugakuNEXT
inventory.region: Planned adjacent to RIKEN's Kobe site, Japan
inventory.claim: RIKEN released the FugakuNEXT basic design report prepared with Fujitsu and NVIDIA. Operation is targeted around 2030.
inventory.limit: The report describes a design and schedule. Installed-system benchmarks and a firm opening date remain undocumented in the sources checked.

trace: riken-fujitsu-fugaku → riken-fujitsu-k-computer: Canonical supersedes link scoped to RIKEN’s shared research installation in Kobe. RIKEN’s 2019 retirement notice describes preparing for the Fugaku installation. MEXT’s 2022 white paper, pp. 242–243, names Fugaku the successor in Japan’s HPCI programme.

riken-fujitsu-fugaku → fujitsu-tofu-interconnect-2: Candidate graph link. Fujitsu traces Fugaku's A64FX-integrated TofuD to Tofu2 in its 2019 FX1000 white paper, pp. 7–8, including new resilience features for densely packed nodes. Dongarra’s technical comparison closely follows the developers’ account.

fujitsu-tofu-interconnect-2 → riken-fujitsu-k-computer: Candidate graph link for the original Tofu design. Fujitsu’s 26 August 2014 Hot Interconnects slides describe a six-dimensional topology and show the controller moving onto the processor chip in Tofu2. The original Tofu also appeared in FX10. Tofu2 was in operation in the FX100-based Plasma Simulator at NIFS in Toki on 1 June 2015. That deployment is an event on the Tofu2 record.

riken-fujitsu-k-computer: RIKEN and Fujitsu reported 10.51 PFlop/s measured LINPACK in 2011. RIKEN began shared use in September 2012 and concluded that service on 16 August 2019, preparing the site for Fugaku’s installation.
alternatives: JUPITER Booster uses Grace Hopper CPU–GPU superchips and InfiniBand NDR with a DragonFly+ topology. This is an implemented alternative to Fugaku's A64FX and TofuD configuration. Jülich's June 2026 technical overview documents its measured FP64 HPL result and the separate CPU module. https://www.fz-juelich.de/en/jsc/jupiter/tech/

The original Tofu design also reached commercial Fujitsu FX10 systems, as the Tofu2 presentation and Ajima et al. §II A record. The separate FX10 installation history remains a lead. https://www.fujitsu.com/downloads/SUPER/ieee/08514929.pdf
frontier: Compare original K/Tofu design documents with non-Fujitsu network design studies to test whether an earlier topology or routing design was explicitly borrowed.
Find a dated Jülich service declaration for the transition from early access to general production for each JUPITER module, with tested user availability.
Check RIKEN’s next operating notice for a verified Fugaku restart and the scope of restored external research access.
screen: Searched current discoveries, source IDs and leads for K computer, Kei, Fugaku/post-K, Tofu, FX100/PRIMEHPC, and JUPITER Booster. No matching canonical machine or Tofu design record or lead was found. Ethernet and CUDA are different referents. No processor fabrication link was inferred.
coverage: Three installations or plans in Japan and Germany, with a single bounded Japanese interconnect lineage. Evidence checked against the 17 November 2026 cutoff. Benchmark results, allocated access, and incident-driven interruption carry separate scopes. Fujitsu supplies the explicit technical inheritance account. The two engineering links remain candidates pending independent informative corroboration. The documented succession concerns the Kobe research installation and shared service.
